problem: Classical ROS navigation pipelines (SLAM + move_base) lack semantic understanding and natural-language interaction, and LLM-based navigation typically needs heavy compute unavailable on low-cost robots.
motivation: Language-guided robots in smart indoor environments need semantic awareness, but low-cost embedded platforms (Jetson Nano, 4 GB) cannot run large models on-board. Splitting perception and control on-board and calling the LLM episodically in the cloud gives a practical, low-cost route.
key_idea: Build a semantic map by anchoring on-board YOLO detections into a LiDAR SLAM metric map, and use a cloud LLM invoked episodically to convert multilingual natural-language commands into structured move_base navigation goals.
insight: A hybrid edge-cloud split works on a low-cost robot: real-time perception and control stay on-board while LLM reasoning costs only about one second per command. The LLM also safely rejects commands referring to objects absent from the semantic map. Evidence is limited to a small single-platform case study with two object classes.
method: LiDAR SLAM + move_base: builds the 2D metric map and executes navigation on ROS 1 Melodic.
YOLO on-board detector: lightweight real-time object detection on the Jetson Nano using RGB-D.
Semantic anchoring: projects detections into the metric map to build a semantic map of object classes and positions.
LLM instruction grounding: cloud LLM interprets natural-language (multilingual) commands and outputs structured navigation goals, rejecting unmapped objects.
Hybrid edge-cloud architecture: perception and control on-board; LLM invoked episodically; detector and nav stack time-multiplexed due to 4 GB memory.

setting.backbone: Cloud LLM (unspecified in abstract, frozen) + lightweight YOLO on Jetson Nano
setting.training_data: none (training-free for the LLM; pretrained YOLO)
setting.action_space: navigation goals executed via ROS move_base (map-frame goal poses)
setting.privileged: none (semantic map built online/pre-built from robot's own detections)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports 10/10 multilingual commands grounded correctly, ~1 s reasoning cost, and one rejected unmapped-object command, but no standard benchmark metrics.
results: In indoor trials over a semantic map of two object classes, all ten multilingual commands were grounded to the correct objects at about one second reasoning cost, and a command for an unmapped object was safely rejected. A single degraded end-to-end trial confirmed the components compose in one session.
limitations: Single-platform case study with only two object classes and ten commands; no standard benchmark or baseline comparison.
4 GB memory forces time-multiplexing of the detector and navigation stack rather than parallel execution.
Depends on cloud connectivity for LLM reasoning.
